name: Continuous firing-path revalidation - a delta column, not a snapshot
description: Blueprint 93 of 96 (design BP-MNT-02). Periodically re-prove that every hook, guard and consumer still FIRES, because registration changes, budget breaches and dependency drift disarm things silently. Mechanism: ACTIVELY TRIGGER a real turn that should exercise each path, then classify the observed evidence into FIRES / INERT / DISARMED / UNREGISTERED / UNKNOWN and DIFF that scorecard against the previous run. The delta is what turns a snapshot into surveillance; a single scorecard cannot tell you anything was lost.

component_inventory.description: ABSOLUTE path to the inventory of hooks, guards and consumers to be probed. An inventory that is itself stale silently shrinks the census.

expected_firing_evidence.description: Per component: the action that SHOULD exercise it and the observable it must leave behind. A component with no declared evidence is UNKNOWN, never assumed firing.

previous_scorecard.description: ABSOLUTE path to the prior scorecard. Without it there is no delta, and without a delta this workflow is a snapshot that cannot detect a regression.

max_concurrency.description: Probe concurrency. Kept modest because several probes contend for the same shared per-turn hook budget, and saturating it would itself disarm checks.

shared_budget_ceiling_ms.description: The shared pre-tool budget. Recording each check's cost against it makes a creeping breach visible BEFORE it disarms something.

trigger-driver.description: Performs the real actions that should exercise each firing path. It does not inspect configuration - configuration is not evidence of firing.

evidence-classifier.description: Classifies each component from observed evidence only, and is required to emit UNKNOWN rather than guess

routes.reason: distinguishing WIRED-BUT-INERT from FIRES is the whole difficulty; the trigger driving is mechanical

stages.title: A stale inventory silently shrinks the census

work_unit.title: Verify the component inventory is current and no component has silently left it
work_unit.question_or_target: Load the inventory and the previous scorecard. Report the inventory's age, its component count, and any component present in the previous scorecard but ABSENT from the inventory - a disappearance from the inventory is indistinguishable from a passing component unless it is named.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: cheap, but a shrinking denominator is the failure mode that makes every later percentage look better

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the inventory path, its mtime, its component count, the previous count, and the named set difference in both directions
tests_required: removing one component from the inventory must be reported as a DISAPPEARANCE, not as a smaller healthy census
an inventory older than the declared window must escalate rather than be used silently
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader who confirms the set difference from the two files directly
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9301 emitted only when both counts and the two-way set difference are recorded; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9301 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - a missing inventory or a missing previous scorecard is a precondition failure, and re-reading the same absent file is not a second signal

stages.title: No census on a stale denominator
TRIGGER each path for real, then look for the observable it should leave

work_unit.title: Trigger one component and record the observable it produced, plus its budget cost
work_unit.question_or_target: Perform the declared trigger for one component and record whether its evidence_marker appeared at evidence_path. Record the check's wallclock contribution to the shared pre-tool budget. Reading the component's registration is NOT a substitute for triggering it.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: driving a real trigger and capturing its side effect

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the trigger performed, the evidence path inspected, the marker found or not found with its byte offset, and the measured cost in ms against the shared ceiling
tests_required: both-states control: deliberately disarm one component and confirm this probe reports its marker ABSENT, then restore it and confirm the marker returns. A probe that reports the same thing in both states measures nothing.
a component that cannot be triggered from a script must record UNKNOWN with the reason, never FIRES
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the evidence classifier reads only the observations, never the trigger driver's opinion of them
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9302 emitted only when the trigger was actually performed and the evidence path inspected; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9302 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: one retry if the trigger itself errored; never retry to turn an ABSENT marker into a present one - that is the finding, not a flake

stages.title: FIRES / INERT / DISARMED / UNREGISTERED / UNKNOWN - five states, not two

work_unit.title: Classify every component from the observations, keeping WIRED-BUT-INERT distinct from FIRES
work_unit.question_or_target: Classify each component: FIRES (marker appeared), INERT (registered and reachable but its feed never writes, so it can never produce a verdict), DISARMED (ran but produced no verdict), UNREGISTERED (absent from the dispatch surface), UNKNOWN (untriggerable). Report the DISARMED count as a first-class metric.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a consumer registered against a feed that never writes is INERT, not healthy - separating those two is judgement over evidence, not a lookup

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per component the class plus the observation that justifies it; for INERT specifically, the evidence that the FEED is cold rather than the consumer broken
tests_required: a consumer whose feed is cold must be classed INERT, not FIRES
a component with no observation must be classed UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN must never be aggregated into a healthy total
the DISARMED count must appear as its own field, not folded into a pass rate
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: none - this stage IS the classifier and holds veto authority; its own output is checked for the UNKNOWN-folded-into-healthy failure mode
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9303 emitted only when every inventory component carries exactly one of the five classes and the DISARMED count is a standalone field; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9303 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - a reclassification over the same observations is not a second signal; a disputed class goes to the delta stage with both readings recorded

stages.title: Configuration is not evidence of firing

work_unit.title: Diff the scorecard against the previous run and name every regression
work_unit.question_or_target: For every component compute delta_since_last. A transition to INERT, DISARMED or UNREGISTERED is a REGRESSION and must be named with both classes. Report the DISARMED count's trend, which matters more than its value.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: deciding which transitions are regressions rather than expected steady states

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per component the previous class, the current class, and the transition verdict; plus the DISARMED count for both runs so the trend is visible rather than asserted
tests_required: a component that moved FIRES -> DISARMED must be named a REGRESSION
a component that moved UNKNOWN -> FIRES must NOT be counted as a regression
both-states control: an identical pair of scorecards must produce zero regressions - a differ that reports regressions on identical input is broken
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader who re-derives at least one transition from the two scorecards directly
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9304 emitted only when every current component has a delta row and the DISARMED trend is recorded for both runs; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9304 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - the diff is deterministic over two files on disk

stages.title: A scorecard with no delta is a snapshot

estimate.measurement_source: 09-WORKFLOW-BLUEPRINT-LIBRARY.md#BP-MNT-02 - the 27-row firing scorecard this program produced as a one-off, including a full check battery found DISARMED

impact.blast_radius: triggers real turns and writes only under command-center/firing/**; the hook and settings trees are explicitly forbid-write so a probe cannot repair what it is measuring

derived_from.credit: owner - the both-states test: a probe silent in both states measures nothing

rollback_to: the one-off 27-row scorecard, produced by hand

x_extensions.mechanism: ACTIVE trigger-then-observe with a five-state classification and a mandatory delta against the previous run. Two things make it more than an audit: WIRED-BUT-INERT is a distinct state from FIRES, and a component that cannot be triggered is UNKNOWN rather than assumed healthy.

not_a_duplicate_because.vs_scheduled-task-liveness-census: that pairs a DECLARATIVE task state with an output-freshness oracle and never triggers anything - it cannot, because a scheduled task's cadence is the subject. This one actively performs the trigger and looks for a side effect. Different instruments, different subjects, and neither can substitute for the other.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_detector-truncation-audit: that compares a reported COUNT against an independent count. This compares an observed FIRING state against the previous run's state.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_live-to-repo-drift-reconcile: that compares file bytes between trees; this compares runtime behaviour between two points in time

contraindications: NOT a functional test of behaviour - it proves a path fires, not that it fires correctly
NOT for third-party hooks you cannot observe - those are UNKNOWN by construction and must be reported as such

benchmark_cases.expect: the DISARMED count moves and the delta names the component; restoring it must move the count back

benchmark_cases.given: a consumer registered against a feed that never writes
benchmark_cases.expect: class INERT, with evidence that the FEED is cold rather than the consumer broken
zero regressions - a differ reporting regressions on identical input is broken

expected_firing_evidence.trigger: end a turn with an uncommitted harness file present
end a turn whose last tool call returned non-zero

scorecard.evidence: consumer reachable; feed last wrote 19 days ago

worked_examples.terminal_state: SUCCESS:BPW-9304 with escalation - 1 regression named, DISARMED trend rising
worked_examples.note: The INERT row is the interesting one: it is STABLE, so a delta-only alarm would stay quiet, and it is UNHEALTHY, so a fires/does-not-fire binary would have called it green. Five states plus a delta is what makes both visible at once.

unverified: That this workflow catches a regression within a month is UNVERIFIED and is the design card's own estimate (very-likely, restated here as likely 55-80% because no run of THIS workflow has happened). Settling experiment = run it twice a week apart and check whether the delta column names anything a single scorecard would have missed.

Whether every declared trigger actually exercises its component is UNVERIFIED per component until the deliberate-disarm control runs for that component. Until then a FIRES verdict rests on the marker appearing, which is a necessary but not sufficient condition.
